QuestionText:
[PASSAGE A: THE SECRET LIFE OF ANTS]
Ants are among the most industrious creatures on Earth. They live in structured colonies consisting of millions of individuals. Each colony is divided into different roles: the queen, whose sole purpose is to lay eggs; workers, who forage for food and maintain the nest; and soldiers, who defend the colony from intruders. Ants communicate using chemicals called pheromones. By leaving a scent trail, an ant can guide its nestmates directly to a discovered food source, such as a drop of spilled honey. This teamwork allows them to carry objects over twenty times their own body weight back to their underground tunnels.

According to the passage, what is the sole purpose of the queen ant?
Options: A) To forage for food
B) To lay eggs
C) To defend the colony
D) To build tunnels
SubTopic: Factual questions — identifying stated information in a passage
Explanation: The text directly states that the queen's 'sole purpose is to lay eggs.'

QuestionText:
[PASSAGE C: THE HISTORY OF THE MARATHON]
Thousands of years ago in ancient Greece, a brave messenger named Pheidippides ran all the way from a battlefield in Marathon to the city of Athens. He carried vital news of a great military victory. He ran approximately 26 miles without stopping. When he arrived, he shouted, 'Victory!' and then collapsed from exhaustion. In 1896, when the modern Olympic Games were started in Athens, organizers created a long-distance running race to honor Pheidippides' historic run. Today, marathons are held all over the world, measuring exactly 26.2 miles, challenging runners to test their absolute limits of endurance.
Options: A) From Marathon to Athens
B) From Athens to Sparta
C) From Rome to Greece
D) From a battlefield to the sea
SubTopic: Factual questions — identifying stated information in a passage
